evidence: Plin. Ep. 5.6.5: semper āēr spīritū aliquō movētur
terms.comment: A Greek word long at home in Latin, as Cicero says; accusative āëra.

terms.gloss: a breath of air, a breeze; in poetry, the air
terms.register: in hōc sēnsū vōx plērumque poētica: Lucr., Verg.
evidence: Plin. Ep. 5.6.5: frequentius tamen aurās quam ventōs habet (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: in the open air, under the open sky
evidence: Cels. 1.2; Suet. Caes. 72; Hor. C. 2.3.23 (Lewis & Short s.v. dīvus)

phrases.latin: terra … circumfūsa undique est hāc animālī spīrābilīque nātūrā, cui nōmen est āēr, Graecum illud quidem sed perceptum jam tamen ūsū ā nostrīs; trītum est enim prō Latīnō
phrases.english: the earth is surrounded on every side by this living, breathable element called aer: a Greek word, but one our people have taken up by use, for it is worn smooth as if it were Latin

phrases.latin: aestātis mīra clēmentia: semper āēr spīritū aliquō movētur
phrases.english: the summer is wonderfully mild: there is always a breath of air stirring

phrases.latin: quid puer Ascanius? superatne et vēscitur aurā?
phrases.english: and the boy Ascanius? Is he alive, does he still breathe the air?
